liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Good Lovin'** (2 reviews): Pigpen is highlighted as conducting the jam section of this song; Transition from Good Lovin' to China Cat Sunflower is called outstanding [4][5]
- Reviewer questions the absence of this song from the recorded setlist [8]
- Song is short because the performance was so intense it nearly burned the venue [12]

## The recordings

- **gd1972-01-02.161838.sbd.anon.gems.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 25 songs; 157 min; rated 2.25/5 by 4 [1]
- **gd72-01-02.sbd.eD.8709.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 25 songs; 139 min; rated 4.65/5 by 46 [2]. Said about its sound: Audio quality is described as phenomenal for a 1972 recording [3]

## Around the show

- Reviewer notes a magical atmosphere at Winterland on the day after New Year's [3]
- Jerry mentions Keith and Donna's first shows at the beginning of set one [6]
- Pigpen wore blue overalls and a cowboy hat while taking charge of the band [14]
- This was the next to last Bay Area appearance for Pigpen [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1972-01-02.161838.sbd.anon.gems.flac16**: transferred by Mastered by Jim Blackwood Speed/pitch adjusted by Jason Chastain Minor repairs, track, FLAC, and pack by Steve Gravel; source: SBD > Master Reel > DAT [1]
- **gd72-01-02.sbd.eD.8709.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [2]. Also: David Gans stated his sources lacked the song, suggesting the recording is complete; Lineage: SBD to Reel Master to Reel to CD to Sonic Solutions; via Charlie Miller [2][9]
